AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Uses of Domestic Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Uses of Domestic Animals.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of Domestic Animals.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Uses of Domestic Animals.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Uses of Domestic Animals.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Making Tacking Stitches? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Making Tacking Stitches.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Making Tacking Stitches.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Making Tacking Stitches.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Making Tacking Stitches.

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fuel Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fuel Conservation.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Fuel Conservation.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fuel Conservation.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fuel Conservation.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds.

10. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Burning crop residue every week

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Fruits? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Growing Fruits.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Fruits.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Fruits.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growing Fruits.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Personal Hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Personal Hygiene.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Personal Hygiene.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Personal Hygiene.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Personal Hygiene.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Personal Hygiene and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Domestic Hygiene and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Making Tacking Stitches and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

2. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. D — Glucose and oxygen

4. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of Domestic Animals.

5. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment.

6. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Making Tacking Stitches.

7. D — 100 °C

8. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fuel Conservation.

9. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds.

10. A — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

11. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Fruits.

12. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Personal Hygiene.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Personal Hygiene; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Domestic Hygiene; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Cleaning Personal Protective Equipment; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Making Tacking Stitches; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
